intro: On the Kayseri–Sivas road, in Kayseri province, stands the largest Seljuk han on that route: Sultan Han, a caravanserai built in 1232–1236. Together with its namesake at Aksaray, it is one of only two built at imperial scale.
history: Sultan Han was built for Alâeddin Keykubad I between 1232 and 1236. It is the largest Seljuk caravanserai on the Kayseri–Sivas road and, with its namesake at Aksaray, one of only two raised at imperial scale. Imagine a caravan arriving here, and everything it needed in one building: a summer court, a covered winter hall, a kiosk mosque and a bath.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the portal and the kiosk mosque. Then step into the covered winter hall, and finish at the bath.
facts: Did you know? The two Sultan Hans follow almost the same plan. When one ruler repeats one building at both ends of a road in the same years, that is a state setting a standard. And together with its namesake at Aksaray, this is one of only two Seljuk hans built at imperial scale.
outro: This brings our journey through Sultan Han, Kayseri to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
